terra-preta.name: Terra preta
terra-preta.summary: A dark, fertile soil found in the Amazon Basin, created by indigenous farmers mixing charcoal, bones, pottery and manure into naturally poor soil, and remaining fertile for thousands of years.

marajoara-culture.name: Marajoara culture
marajoara-culture.summary: An ancient culture that flourished on Marajó island at the mouth of the Amazon in Brazil, with human activity documented as early as 1000 BCE.

maraj.name: Marajó
maraj.summary: A large island in Pará, Brazil, at the mouth of the Amazon, site from roughly 400 BCE to 1600 CE of the advanced pre-Cabraline Marajoara society.

astrocaryum-vulgare.name: Tucuma
astrocaryum-vulgare.summary: A very spiny palm native to the Amazon and the Guianas with edible fruit, which thrives in deforested land rather than undisturbed rainforest.

maloca.name: Maloca
maloca.summary: Traditional Amazonian long house shared by several families, with separate entrances for men and women and space cleared for ceremonial dances.

anna-curtenius-roosevelt.name: Anna Roosevelt
anna-curtenius-roosevelt.summary: American archaeologist (born 1946) and leading researcher of Paleoindians in the Amazon basin, known for excavations at Marajó Island and Caverna da Pedra Pintada; great-granddaughter of Theodore Roosevelt.

charles-c-mann.name: Charles C. Mann
charles-c-mann.summary: American journalist and author (born 1955) whose 2006 book on the pre-Columbian Americas won a major book award.

casarabe-culture.name: Casarabe culture
casarabe-culture.summary: A pre-Columbian civilization (c. 500–1400 AD) in Bolivia's Amazon lowlands that built large earthen platforms and pyramids, revealed by lidar surveys led by archaeologist Heiko Prümers.

tiwanaku.name: Tiwanaku
tiwanaku.summary: A major pre-Columbian archaeological site in Bolivia near Lake Titicaca, home to an estimated 10,000 to 20,000 people around 800 CE, with monumental structures and megalithic stonework.

llanos-de-moxos.name: Llanos de Moxos
llanos-de-moxos.summary: A tropical savanna ecoregion of the Beni Department of northern Bolivia, also known as the Beni savanna.

cotoca.name: Cotoca
cotoca.summary: A municipality in Bolivia's Santa Cruz Department, home since 1799 to a shrine to the Virgen de Cotoca, now patron saint of the whole province.

betty-meggers.name: Betty Meggers
betty-meggers.summary: American archaeologist (1921-2012) best known for her work in South America and long association with the Smithsonian Institution, who wrote extensively on environment as a shaper of human cultures.

mapuche.name: Mapuche
mapuche.summary: An Indigenous people of south-central Chile and southwestern Argentina, with a traditional economy based on agriculture and material culture known for textiles and silverwork.

puquina-language.name: Puquina language
puquina-language.summary: An extinct language once spoken around Lake Titicaca in Peru and Bolivia, associated with the Tiwanaku culture and still an official language of Bolivia, known mainly from a single 1607 document.

matrilocal-residence.name: Matrilocal residence
matrilocal-residence.summary: A social system in which a married couple lives with or near the wife's family, rather than the husband's.
